3133.text: The reaction $X \rightarrow$ products is a first order reaction. In 40 minutes, the concentration of $X$ changes from $1.0 \mathrm{M}$ to $0.25 \mathrm{M}$. What is the initial rate of reaction when $[X]=0.1 \mathrm{M}$ ? $(\log 4=0.60)$
3133.sol:
Given, (concentration) $a=1.0 \mathrm{M}, a-x=0.25 \mathrm{M}, t=40$ minutes For a first order reaction, $\begin{aligned} k & =\frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{a}{a-x}\\
& =\frac{2.303}{40} \log \frac{1}{0.25}=\frac{2.303}{40} \log4 \\
& =\frac{2.303 \times 2 \times 0.3010}{40}\\
& =0.03466 \mathrm{ min}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$ Now, Initial rate $\begin{aligned}& =k[A] \\
& =0.03466(0.1) \\
& =0.003466 \mathrm{ mol}/ \mathrm{L}/ \mathrm\min\\
& =3.466 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{ mol}/ \mathrm{L}/ \mathrm\min\\
& =3.47 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{ mol}/ \mathrm{L}/ \mathrm\min
\end{aligned}$ According to options given, any option cannot match with answer. But (d) can be the correct answer.

3432.subject: Chemistry
3432.text:
Which complex among the following has the highest value of spin only magnetic moment?
\(\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-},\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-},\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}\), $(\left[\mathrm{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\)$
3432.sol:
(a) \($\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_$6\right]^{3-}\) has \(d² s p³\) (inner \(d\) - complex) hybridisation with one electron unpaired. (b) The \($\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) ion in \($\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_$6\right]^{4-}\) has outer electronic configuration of \(3 d⁶\). The complex is a low spin complex. It contains 0 unpaired electrons with magnetic moment of \(0 $\mathrm{BM}$\) Therefore, under the influence of the octahedral crystal field, the possible electronic arrangement of \($\mathrm{Fe}$\) (II) ion is \(t_{2 g}^6, e_g^0\). (c) \($\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_$4\right]^{2-}\) is a square planar geometry formed by \(d s p²\) hybridisation. \($\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_$4\right]^{2-}\) is diamagnetic, so \($\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$\) ion has \(3 d⁸\), outer configuration with two unpaired electrons. For the formation of the square planar sructure by structure by \(d s p²\) - hybridisation, two unpaired \(d\)-electrons are paired up due to energy made available by the approach of ligands, making one of the \(3 d\)-orbitals empty.
\(\therefore $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$\)is a weak ligand so, there is no pairing of electrons. Number of unpaired \(=2\) Hence, the correct option is (d).

5634.subject: Chemistry
5634.text: The element with outer electronic configuration $( n - 1 ) d^{2}ns^{2}$, where $n = 4$, would belong to
5634.sol:
We know that the general configuration of& $d -$block element is~$( n - 1 ) d^{1 - 10}{ns}^{1 - 2}$~where& $n$~is the period number.

Here given& electronic configuration is& $( n - 1 ) d^{2}{ns}^{2}$, where~$n = 4$. So, here the period number will be~$4$.

For~$d -$block elements the group number can be found by adding no of electrons in~$\left(n - 1\right)d$~sub-shell and the no of electrons present in the& $ns$~sub-shell.

So, here group number will be& $2 + 2 = 4$.

Hence, the element belongs to ${4}^{th }$ period and~${4}^{th }$ group

6111.subject: Mathematics
6111.text: If the tangent drawn to the curve $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}^3$ at a point $(\alpha, \beta)$ cuts again the curve at another point $\left(\alpha_1, \beta_1\right)$, then $\frac{\beta_1}{\beta}=$
6111.sol:
$\because y=x^3$
Equation of tangent line at point $(\alpha, \beta)$ is:
$(y-\beta)=3 \alpha^2(x-\alpha)$
$\because\left(\alpha_1, \beta_1\right)$ 
lies on equation (i), we get
$\beta_1-\beta=3 \alpha^2\left(\alpha_1-\alpha\right)$
$\begin{array}{r}\Rightarrow \alpha_1^3-\alpha^3=3 \alpha^2\left(\alpha_1-\alpha\right) \\ \left\{\because\left(\alpha_1, \beta_1\right) \&(\alpha, \beta) \text{ lies on } y=x^3\right\}\end{array}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\alpha_1^3}{\alpha^3}-1=3\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}-1\right) \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}\right)^3-3 \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}+2=0$
Let $y=\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}$
Then, $y^3-3 y+2=0 \Rightarrow(y-1)^2(y+2)=0$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}-1\right)^2\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}+2\right)=0 \\ & \because \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}-1=0 \text{ or } \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}=2 \\ & \alpha_1=\alpha \text{ (not possible) or } \frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}\right)^3=-8\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{\beta_1}{\beta}=\frac{\alpha_1^3}{\alpha^3}=\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha}\right)^3=-8$

$⇒ A = 0, B = 1, C = 0, D = 22, E = 0, F = 5$

7787.sol:
Given that

${∫}_{- 1 / 2}^{1 / 2}\left\{[ x ] + log ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)\right\}dx$

Let $f\left(x\right) = log\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right) ⇒ f\left(- x\right) = log\left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}\right)$

$f\left(- x\right) = log{\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)}^{- 1} ⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - log\left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

So $f\left(x\right)$ is an odd function $⇒ {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}f\left(x\right) d x = 0; f\left(- x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

${∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\left[x\right]dx = {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{0}\left[x\right]dx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}\left[x\right]dx$

$= {∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{0} - 1dx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}0dx$

$= {\left[- x\right]}_{\dfrac{- 1}{2}}^{0}$

$= \dfrac{- 1}{2} .$

$∴ {∫}_{- 1 / 2}^{1 / 2}\left\{[ x ] + log ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1 + x}{1 - x}\right)\right\}dx = \dfrac{- 1}{2} .$

& a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right) \\

\Rightarrow \quad & a \tan ^{-1} x+b \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} x \\
\Rightarrow \quad & a=-\frac{1}{2}, \quad b=\frac{1}{4} \\
\therefore \quad & a-2 b=-\frac{1}{2}-2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=-1
\end{aligned}$

10178.text: The point of intersection of the latus rectum and axis of the parabola ${y}^{2} + 4x + 2y - 8 = 0$ is
10178.sol:
The point of intersection of the latus rectum and axis of the parabola ${y}^{2} + 4x + 2y - 8 = 0$ is the focus of the parabola.

${y}^{2} + 4x + 2y - 8 = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} + 2y + 1 = - 4x + 8 + 1$

$⇒ {\left(y + 1\right)}^{2} = 4\left(- 1\right)\left(x - \dfrac{9}{4}\right)$

We know that the focus of the parabola ${\left(y - k\right)}^{2} = 4a\left(x - h\right)$ is $S ≡ \left(a + h, k\right)$.

So, the focus of the given parabola is $S ≡ \left(- 1 + \dfrac{9}{4}, - 1\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{4}, - 1\right)$.

19855.subject: Chemistry
19855.text: The initial pressure of the system before decomposition for a first order gas phase reaction $A_{(g)} \rightarrow B_{(g)} + C_{(g)}$ was $P_i$. After lapse of time 't', total pressure of the system increased by 'x' units and became $P_t$. The rate constant 'k' for the reaction is given as:
19855.sol:
The given gas phase reaction is $A_{(g)} \rightarrow B_{(g)} + C_{(g)}$.

At $t = 0$, the initial pressure is $P_i$.
Pressure of $A = P_i$, Pressure of $B = 0$, Pressure of $C = 0$.

At time $t$, let the pressure of $A$ decrease by $x$.
Pressure of $A = P_i - x$
Pressure of $B = x$
Pressure of $C = x$

Total pressure at time $t$ is $P_t = (P_i - x) + x + x = P_i + x$.
From this, we get $x = P_t - P_i$.

The partial pressure of reactant $A$ at time $t$ is:
$P_A = P_i - x = P_i - (P_t - P_i) = 2P_i - P_t$

For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:
$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{P_A}$

Substituting the value of $P_A$:
$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{2P_i - P_t}$

Answer: $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log\dfrac{P_i}{2P_i - P_t}$

20920.subject: Mathematics
20920.text: If the function $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, then the value of '$a$' is ___ and the function attains a ___ at $ x = 1$
20920.sol:
Given $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 4x^3 - 62x + a$

Since $f(x)$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, $f'(1) = 0$

$4(1)^3 - 62(1) + a = 0$

$a = 58$

Now, finding the second derivative:

$f''(x) = 12x^2 - 62$

At $x = 1$, $f''(1) = 12(1)^2 - 62 = -50$

Since $f''(1) < 0$, the function attains a local maxima at $x = 1$.

Answer: $a = 58$ , local maxima

22049.subject: Mathematics
22049.text: A relation $R$ is defined from $\{2,3,4\}$ to $\{3,6,7,10\}$. If $x R y \Leftrightarrow x$ and $y$ are co prime numbers. Then range of $R$ is
22049.sol:
The relation $R$ is defined from the set $A = \{2, 3, 4\}$ to the set $B = \{3, 6, 7, 10\}$ such that $x R y$ if and only if $x$ and $y$ are coprime, meaning $\gcd(x, y) = 1$.

We check each element of $A$ against each element of $B$:

For $x = 2$:
$\gcd(2,3) = 1$ (coprime)
$\gcd(2,6) = 2$ (not coprime)
$\gcd(2,7) = 1$ (coprime)
$\gcd(2,10) = 2$ (not coprime)
So, $2 R 3$ and $2 R 7$.

For $x = 3$:
$\gcd(3,3) = 3$ (not coprime)
$\gcd(3,6) = 3$ (not coprime)
$\gcd(3,7) = 1$ (coprime)
$\gcd(3,10) = 1$ (coprime)
So, $3 R 7$ and $3 R 10$.

For $x = 4$:
$\gcd(4,3) = 1$ (coprime)
$\gcd(4,6) = 2$ (not coprime)
$\gcd(4,7) = 1$ (coprime)
$\gcd(4,10) = 2$ (not coprime)
So, $4 R 3$ and $4 R 7$.

The set of all elements $y \in B$ such that there exists $x \in A$ with $x R y$ is the range of $R$.
The elements $y$ that satisfy the condition are $3, 7, 10$.
Therefore, the range of $R$ is $\{3, 7, 10\}$.

Answer: $\{3,7,10\}$

22208.subject: Mathematics
22208.text: The point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-4}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=z$ is
22208.sol:
Let the first line be $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{3} = \dfrac{z-3}{4} = s$. Then the coordinates of any point on this line are $(2s+1, 3s+2, 4s+3)$.

Let the second line be $\dfrac{x-4}{5} = \dfrac{y-1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{1} = t$. Then the coordinates of any point on this line are $(5t+4, 2t+1, t)$.

For the lines to intersect, there must exist values of $s$ and $t$ such that the coordinates are equal:
$2s+1 = 5t+4 \Rightarrow 2s - 5t = 3$
$3s+2 = 2t+1 \Rightarrow 3s - 2t = -1$
$4s+3 = t$

Substituting $t = 4s+3$ into the first equation:
$2s - 5(4s+3) = 3 \Rightarrow 2s - 20s - 15 = 3 \Rightarrow -18s = 18 \Rightarrow s = -1$.

Substituting $s = -1$ into $t = 4s+3$:
$t = 4(-1) + 3 = -1$.

Checking these values in the second equation:
$3(-1) - 2(-1) = -3 + 2 = -1$. This matches the equation $3s - 2t = -1$.

The point of intersection is obtained by substituting $s = -1$ into the first line coordinates:
$x = 2(-1) + 1 = -1$
$y = 3(-1) + 2 = -1$
$z = 4(-1) + 3 = -1$.

The point of intersection is $(-1, -1, -1)$.

Answer: $(-1,-1,-1)$

22817.subject: Physics
22817.text: An electric field $E=3 x^2 i N C^{-1}$ exists in a certain region of space. The potential difference between the origin and at $x=4 m, V_0-V_4$ is
22817.sol:
The relationship between electric field $\vec{E}$ and electric potential $V$ is given by $dV = -\vec{E} \cdot d\vec{r}$.

Given $\vec{E} = 3x^2 \hat{i}$, we have $dV = -3x^2 dx$.

To find the potential difference $V_0 - V_4$, we integrate from $x=4$ to $x=0$:

$V_0 - V_4 = \int_{4}^{0} -3x^2 dx$.

$V_0 - V_4 = -3 \int_{4}^{0} x^2 dx$.

$V_0 - V_4 = -3 \left[ \dfrac{x^3}{3} \right]_{4}^{0}$.

$V_0 - V_4 = -[x^3]_{4}^{0} = -(0^3 - 4^3) = -(-64) = 64 \text{ V}$.

Answer: 64 V

23042.text: A straight wire of length $2 \mathrm{ m}$ carries a current of $10 \mathrm{ A}$. If this wire is placed in uniform magnetic field of $0.15 \mathrm{ T}$ making an angle of $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the magnetic field, the applied force on the wire will be

Given values are:
$I = 10 \text{ A}$
$L = 2 \text{ m}$
$B = 0.15 \text{ T}$
$\theta = 45^{{}^{\circ}}$

Substituting these values into the formula:
$F = 10 \times 2 \times 0.15 \times \sin(45^{{}^{\circ}})$

$F = 20 \times 0.15 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$F = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ N}$

Answer: $3 / \sqrt{2} \mathrm{ N}$

23386.subject: Physics
23386.text: A plane glass mirror of thickness 3 cm of material of $\mu = \frac{3}{2}$ is silvered on the back surface. When a point object is placed 9 cm from the front surface of the mirror, then the position of the brightest image from the front surface is
23386.sol:
The brightest image is formed by light that refracts into the glass, reflects from the silvered back surface, and refracts back out.

Refraction at front surface: Apparent distance of object from front surface as seen inside glass:
$u' = \mu \times u = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 9 = 13.5$ cm

Reflection at silvered back surface: Distance of apparent object from back mirror $= 13.5 + 3 = 16.5$ cm

Plane mirror forms image 16.5 cm behind the back surface. Distance of this image from the front surface (inside glass) $= 16.5 + 3 = 19.5$ cm

Refraction back out at front surface: Final apparent distance from front surface as seen in air:
$v' = \dfrac{v}{\mu} = \dfrac{19.5}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = 19.5 \times \dfrac{2}{3} = 13$ cm

A block of mass $2M$ is attached to a massless spring with spring-constant $k .$ This block is connected to two other blocks of masses $M$ and $2M$ using two massless pulleys and strings. Equivalent mass

$= \dfrac{2\left(2m\right) \times m}{2m + m} = \dfrac{4m}{3}$
$⇒ T = \left(\dfrac{4m}{3}\right) . g$
$∴ 2T = 2 . \dfrac{4mg}{3} = \left(\dfrac{8m}{3}\right)g$
$⇒ {m}_{eq} = \dfrac{8m}{3}$

Using mechanical energy conservation

Consider the effect of only the electrical force on the particle. Then the maximum speed, in $m{s}^{- 1}$, attained by the particle at subsequent times is ____________.

$m = {10}^{- 3}kg, q = 1C, t = 0$
Force on particle will be
$F = qE = q{E}_{0}sin\left(\omegat\right)$
At ${v}_{max}, F = 0$ $⇒ q{E}_{0}sin ⁡ \omega{t}_{o} = 0$
$⇒ \omega{t}_{o} = \pi$
$F = q{E}_{0}sin ⁡ \omegat$
$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = q\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{m}sin\left(\omegat\right)$
${∫}_{0}^{v}dv = {∫}_{0}^{\pi ∕ \omega}\dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m}sin\left(\omegat\right)dt$
$v - 0 = \dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m\omega}{\left[- cos\left(\omegat\right)\right]}_{0}^{\pi ∕ \omega}$
$v - 0 = \dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m\omega}\left[\left(- cos\left(\pi\right)\right) - \left(- cos\left(0\right)\right)\right]$
$v = \dfrac{1 \times 1}{m\omega} \times 2 = 2 m {s}^{- 1}$

26485.subject: Physics
26485.text: A particle of mass $1kg$ is subjected to a force which depends on the position as $\overset{\to}{F} = - k\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right)kgm{s}^{- 2}$ with $k = 1kg{s}^{- 2}$. At time $t = 0$, the particle's position $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)m$ and its velocity $\overset{\to}{v} = \left(- \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{2}{\pi}\overset{^}{k}\right)m{s}^{- 1}$. Let ${v}_{x} and {v}_{y}$ denote the $x$ and the $y$ components of the particle's velocity, respectively. Ignore gravity. When $z = 0 . 5m$, the value of $\left(x{v}_{y} - y{v}_{x}\right)$ is ______ ${m}^{2}{s}^{- 1}$.
26485.sol:
Given here: $\overset{\to}{F} = - k\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right)kgm{s}^{- 2}$ and $m = 1kg$

In x-direction, ${F}_{x} = - x = m{a}_{x}$

So, acceleration, ${a}_{x} = \dfrac{{d}^{2}x}{d{t}^{2}} = - x$

Now, for particle executing SHM, displacement along x-direction is

$⇒ x = {A}_{x}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$, here, angular frequency, $\omega = 1rad{s}^{- 1}$ and velocity, ${v}_{x} = {A}_{x}\omegacos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$

Given at $t = 0, x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}m$ and ${v}_{x} = - \sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, putting the values, we get

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = {A}_{x}sin{ϕ}_{x}$ and $- \sqrt{2} = {A}_{x}cos{ϕ}_{x}$

From above two equations,

$⇒ tan{ϕ}_{x} = - \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

And ${A}_{x} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}m . . . \left(2\right)$

Similarly, along y-direction,

${F}_{y} = - y = m{a}_{y}$,

$⇒ {a}_{y} = \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{t}^{2}} = - y$

So, displacement, $y = {A}_{y}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right)$ and velocity ${v}_{y} = {A}_{y}\omegacos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right)$

Given at $t = 0, y = \sqrt{2}m$ and ${v}_{y} = \sqrt{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

So, putting the values, we get

$\sqrt{2} = {A}_{y}sin{ϕ}_{y}$ and $\sqrt{2} = {A}_{y}cos{ϕ}_{y}$

From above two relations, we have

$⇒ {ϕ}_{y} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} . . . \left(3\right)$ and ${A}_{y} = 2m . . . \left(4\right)$

Now, the value of $\left(x{v}_{y} - y{v}_{x}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right) \times 2cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) - 2sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) \times \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} \times 2\left(sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) - sin\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{y}\right) \times cos\left(\omegat + {ϕ}_{x}\right)\right)

$= \sqrt{10}sin\left({ϕ}_{x} - {ϕ}_{y}\right)$

$= \sqrt{10}\left(sin{ϕ}_{x}cos{ϕ}_{y} - cos{ϕ}_{x}sin{ϕ}_{y}\right)$

$= \sqrt{10}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \left(- \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right) \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

$= 3$

26633.subject: Physics
26633.text:
As shown in the figure, an insulated container is fitted with a thermally conducting but immovable partition $(P_1)$ and a freely movable but thermally insulated piston $(P_2)$. The partition $P_1$ with thermal conductivity $K$, cross sectional area $A$ and width $x$ divides the container into two sections, $S_1$ and $S_2$, each containing one mole of a monoatomic gas. The piston $P_2$ moves freely such that the gas in $S_2$ is always at the atmospheric pressure. Initially, the difference between the temperatures of $S_1$ and $S_2$ is $\Delta T_0$. The time it takes for the temperature difference to become $\dfrac{\Delta T_0}{2}$ is $n x R / K A$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant. The value of $n$ is:
[Given: $\ln 2 \approx 0.7$]
26633.sol:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be the temperatures of the gases in sections $S_1$ and $S_2$ respectively. Assume $T_1 > T_2$, so heat flows from $S_1$ to $S_2$.

The rate of heat transfer through the partition $P_1$ is given by Fourier's law of heat conduction:
$\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{KA}{x} (T_1 - T_2)$

For section $S_1$, the volume is constant (since $P_1$ is immovable). Thus, the process is isochoric. The heat lost by $S_1$ is:
$dQ = -n_1 C_V dT_1$
Since the gas is monoatomic and $n_1 = 1$ mole, $C_V = \dfrac{3}{2}R$.
$\Rightarrow dT_1 = -\dfrac{2 dQ}{3R}$

For section $S_2$, the pressure is constant (since $P_2$ is freely movable and exposed to atmospheric pressure). Thus, the process is isobaric. The heat gained by $S_2$ is:
$dQ = n_2 C_P dT_2$
Since the gas is monoatomic and $n_2 = 1$ mole, $C_P = \dfrac{5}{2}R$.
$\Rightarrow dT_2 = \dfrac{2 dQ}{5R}$

The change in the temperature difference $d(\Delta T) = d(T_1 - T_2)$ is:
$d(T_1 - T_2) = dT_1 - dT_2 = -\dfrac{2 dQ}{3R} - \dfrac{2 dQ}{5R} = -\dfrac{16 dQ}{15R}$

Substituting the rate of heat transfer $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ into the equation:
$\dfrac{d(T_1 - T_2)}{dt} = -\dfrac{16}{15R} \left( \dfrac{KA}{x} (T_1 - T_2) \right)$

Let $\Delta T = T_1 - T_2$. The differential equation becomes:
$\dfrac{d(\Delta T)}{\Delta T} = -\dfrac{16 KA}{15 R x} dt$

Integrating both sides from $t = 0$ to $t$, where the temperature difference goes from $\Delta T_0$ to $\dfrac{\Delta T_0}{2}$:
$\int_{\Delta T_0}^{\Delta T_0 / 2} \dfrac{d(\Delta T)}{\Delta T} = -\dfrac{16 KA}{15 R x} \int_0^t dt$

$\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{16 KA}{15 R x} t$

$-\ln 2 = -\dfrac{16 KA}{15 R x} t$

$t = \dfrac{15 R x \ln 2}{16 KA}$

Given that $\ln 2 \approx 0.7$:
$t = \dfrac{15 \times 0.7}{16} \dfrac{x R}{KA} = \dfrac{10.5}{16} \dfrac{x R}{KA} = \dfrac{21}{32} \dfrac{x R}{KA} = 0.65625 \dfrac{x R}{KA}$

Comparing this with the given expression $t = n \dfrac{x R}{K A}$, we get:
$n = 0.65625$

Answer: $0.66$

Rate $= k[ A ][ B ]$

$⇒ 2R = {R}^{'}$ i.e, rate become doubles.

29130.subject: Chemistry
29130.text: The correct order of basicity of oxides of vanadium is
29130.sol:
${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$:~In,& ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$, the oxidation state of~$\text{V}$~is as follows

$2 ( x ) + 3 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x - 6 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$

The oxidation state of~$V$~in& ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$~is +3. The vanadium is present in its lowest oxidation state. The vanadium tends to donate the pair of electrons. Hence, it is basic oxide.

${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$:~In& ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$, the oxidation state of~$V$~is as follows

$2 ( x ) + 5 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2 ( x ) - 10 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5$

The oxidation state of~$V$~in& ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$~is +5.& The Vanadium tends to donate and accept the pair of electrons.& It is amphoteric oxide.

${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$:~In& ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$, the oxidation state of~$V$~is as follows

$2 ( x ) + 4 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2 ( x ) - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{8}{2} = 4$

The oxidation state of~$V$~in& ${V}_{2}{O}_{4}$~is +4.& The Vanadium is present in its other low oxidation state.& The Vanadium tends to donate and accept the pair of electrons.& It is amphoteric oxide and less basic than& ${V}_{2}{O}_{3}$, more basic than~${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$.

So, the correct order of basicity of oxides of vanadium is~${V}_{2}{O}_{3} > {V}_{2}{O}_{4} > {V}_{2}{O}_{5}$.

29136.subject: Chemistry
29136.text:
The set of correct statements is:

(i) Manganese exhibits $+ 7$ oxidation state in its oxide.

(ii) Ruthenium and Osmium exhibit $+ 8$ oxidation in their oxides.

(iii) $Sc$ shows $+ 4$ oxidation state which is oxidizing in nature.

(iv) $Cr$ shows oxidising nature in $+ 6$ oxidation state.
29136.sol:
(i) The oxidation state of $Mn$ in oxide (${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$) is:

Let us consider $Mn$ as $x$.

$⇒ 2x + 7 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x + ( - 14 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x - 14 = 0$

$⇒ 2x = 14$

$⇒ x = 7$

(ii) The oxidation state of Ruthenium in oxide (${RuO}_{4}$) is:

Consider $Ru$ as $x$.

$⇒ x + 4 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$

The oxidation state of Osmium in oxide (${OsO}_{4}$) is:

Consider $Os$ as $x$.

$⇒ x + 4 ( - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$

Hence, Ruthenium and Osmium has +7 oxidation state in its oxide.

(iii) $Sc$ has ${ns}^{2} ( n - 1 ) {d}^{1}$ electronic configuration.

It utilizes two electrons from its $ns$ sub-shell then its oxidation state = +2. When it utilizes both the electrons then its oxidation state = +3.

(iv) In the modern periodic table, chromium metal is present in group 6. It is a transition metal and belongs to the first transition series. The atomic number of chromium is 24. Its electronic configuration is $[ Ar ] 3{d}^{5}4{s}^{1}$.

It has five electrons in the 3d sub-shell and one electron in the 4s sub-shell. Thus, chromium metal has six valence electrons. Chromium can lose some or all of its valence electrons to form ions with different oxidation states. Thus, chromium shows the oxidation states of +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, and +6 respectively.
The most common oxidation states of chromium are +2, +3, and +6.

So, the statement (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

32162.subject: Chemistry
32162.text:
The surface of sodium metal is irradiated with radiation of wavelength $x$ nm. The kinetic energy of ejected electrons is $2.8 \times 10^{-20}$ J. The work function of sodium is $2.3$ eV. The value of $x$ is _____ $\times 10^2$ nm. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}$ J s; $1$ eV $= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J; $c = 3.0 \times 10^8$ m s$^{-1}$)
32162.sol:
The work function of sodium in Joules is:

$\Phi = 2.3 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = 3.68 \times 10^{-19}$ J

The kinetic energy of the ejected electrons is:

$K = 2.8 \times 10^{-20} = 0.28 \times 10^{-19}$ J

Using the photoelectric equation, the energy of the incident photon is:

$E = \Phi + K$

$E = 3.68 \times 10^{-19} + 0.28 \times 10^{-19} = 3.96 \times 10^{-19}$ J

The wavelength of the incident radiation is calculated using $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{E} = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.0 \times 10^8}{3.96 \times 10^{-19}}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{19.8 \times 10^{-26}}{3.96 \times 10^{-19}} = 5 \times 10^{-7}$ m

Converting the wavelength to nanometers:

$\lambda = 500 \times 10^{-9}$ m $= 500$ nm

Given that the wavelength is $x$ nm, we get $x = 500$.

Expressing $x$ in the required format:

$x = 5 \times 10^2$

The value to be filled in the blank is $5$.

Answer: $5$

35103.subject: Mathematics
35103.text: If the domain of the function $f(x) = \sqrt{\log_{(0.6)}\left(\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4}\right|\right)}$ is $(-\infty, a] \cup \{b\} \cup [c, d) \cup (e, \infty)$, then the value of $a + b + c + d + e$ is _______.
35103.sol:
For the function $f(x) = \sqrt{\log_{0.6}\left(\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4} ight| ight)}$ to be defined, two conditions must be satisfied:

1. The argument of the logarithm must be strictly positive:
$\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4} ight| > 0 \implies 2x - 5 eq 0 \implies x eq \dfrac{5}{2}$
Also, the denominator cannot be zero:
$x^2 - 4 eq 0 \implies x eq \pm 2$

2. The expression inside the square root must be non-negative:
$\log_{0.6}\left(\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4} ight| ight) \ge 0$

Since the base of the logarithm is $0.6 < 1$, the inequality sign reverses when removing the logarithm:
$\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4} ight| \le (0.6)^0$
$\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4} ight| \le 1$

Since both sides are non-negative, we can square both sides:
$(2x-5)^2 \le (x^2-4)^2$
$(x^2-4)^2 - (2x-5)^2 \ge 0$

Using the identity $A^2 - B^2 = (A-B)(A+B)$:
$(x^2 - 4 - 2x + 5)(x^2 - 4 + 2x - 5) \ge 0$
$(x^2 - 2x + 1)(x^2 + 2x - 9) \ge 0$
$(x - 1)^2 (x^2 + 2x - 9) \ge 0$

Since $(x - 1)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, the inequality holds if:
$x - 1 = 0 \implies x = 1$
or
$x^2 + 2x - 9 \ge 0$

Finding the roots of $x^2 + 2x - 9 = 0$ using the quadratic formula:
$x = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(1)(-9)}}{2} = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{40}}{2} = -1 \pm \sqrt{10}$

Thus, $x^2 + 2x - 9 \ge 0$ gives:
$x \in (-\infty, -1 - \sqrt{10}] \cup [-1 + \sqrt{10}, \infty)$

Combining this with $x = 1$, the solution to the inequality is:
$x \in (-\infty, -1 - \sqrt{10}] \cup \{1\} \cup [-1 + \sqrt{10}, \infty)$

Now, we must exclude the restricted values $x = \pm 2 and x = \dfrac{5}{2}$.
Note that $-1 - \sqrt{10} \approx -4.16$ and $-1 + \sqrt{10} \approx 2.16$.
The values $-2 and 2$ do not fall in the above intervals, so they are already excluded.
However, $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5$, which lies in the interval $[-1 + \sqrt{10}, \infty)$. We must exclude it by splitting the interval:
$[-1 + \sqrt{10}, \dfrac{5}{2}) \cup (\dfrac{5}{2}, \infty)$

The final domain of the function is:
$(-\infty, -1 - \sqrt{10}] \cup \{1\} \cup [-1 + \sqrt{10}, \dfrac{5}{2}) \cup (\dfrac{5}{2}, \infty)$

Comparing this with the given domain $(-\infty, a] \cup \{b\} \cup [c, d) \cup (e, \infty)$, we get:
$a = -1 - \sqrt{10}$
$b = 1$
$c = -1 + \sqrt{10}$
$d = \dfrac{5}{2}$
$e = \dfrac{5}{2}$

We need to find the value of $a + b + c + d + e$:
$a + b + c + d + e = (-1 - \sqrt{10}) + 1 + (-1 + \sqrt{10}) + \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2}$
$= -1 - \sqrt{10} + 1 - 1 + \sqrt{10} + 5$
$= 4$

Answer: $4$

38518.text:
Let for a triangle $ABC$

$\overset{\to}{AB} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{CB} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{CA} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k}$

If $\delta > 0$ and the area of the triangle $ABC$ is $5\sqrt{6}$ then $\overset{\to}{CB} \cdot \overset{\to}{CA}$ is equal to
38518.sol:
Given,

A triangle $ABC$

$\overset{\to}{AB} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{CB} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{CA} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k}$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Now from triangle law of addition we get,

$\overset{\to}{CA} + \overset{\to}{AB} = \overset{\to}{CB}$

$⇒ 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k} + \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \left(\delta + 3\right)\overset{^}{k} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$\alpha = 2, \beta = 4 \text{ and } \gamma = \delta + 3$

Now area of triangle is given by,

$A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{BC}\right|$

$⇒ 5\sqrt{6} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & \gamma\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ {\left(5\sqrt{6}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\gamma - 12\right)}^{2} + {\left(6 + 2\gamma\right)}^{2} + 100$

$⇒ 5{\gamma}^{2} = 320$

$⇒ {\gamma}^{2} = 64 ⇒ \gamma = 8$

So, $\delta = 8 - 3 = 5$

$\overset{\to}{CB} \cdot \overset{\to}{CA} = \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \delta\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{CB} \cdot \overset{\to}{CA} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 8\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) = 8 + 12 + 40 = 60$

40123.subject: Physics
40123.text:
In the given circuit below inductance values of $L_1$, $L_2$ and $L_3$ are same. The magnetic energy stored in the entire circuit is $(U_t)$ and that stored in the $L_2$ inductor is $(U_l)$. $U_t / U_l$ is __________.
(Ignore the mutual inductance if any)
40123.sol:
Let the inductance of each inductor be $L$, so $L_1 = L_2 = L_3 = L$.

Let the total current flowing through the circuit be $I$. This current flows entirely through $L_1$.

Since $L_2$ and $L_3$ are connected in parallel and have equal inductances, the current $I$ divides equally between them. Therefore, the current through $L_2$ is $\dfrac{I}{2}$ and the current through $L_3$ is $\dfrac{I}{2}$.

The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is given by $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L i^2$.

The energy stored in the inductor $L_2$ is:
$U_l = \dfrac{1}{2} L \left(\dfrac{I}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{8} L I^2$

The equivalent inductance of the entire circuit is:
$L_{eq} = L_1 + \dfrac{L_2 L_3}{L_2 + L_3} = L + \dfrac{L \cdot L}{L + L} = L + \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{3L}{2}$

The total magnetic energy stored in the entire circuit is:
$U_t = \dfrac{1}{2} L_{eq} I^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{3L}{2}\right) I^2 = \dfrac{3}{4} L I^2$

The ratio of the total energy to the energy stored in $L_2$ is:
$\dfrac{U_t}{U_l} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{4} L I^2}{\dfrac{1}{8} L I^2} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 8 = 6$

Answer: $6$

40152.text: A coil of $200$ turns and area $0 . 20{m}^{2}$ is rotated at half a revolution per second and is placed in uniform magnetic field of $0 . 01T$ perpendicular to axis of rotation of the coil. The maximum voltage generated in the coil is $\dfrac{2\pi}{\beta}$ volt. The value of $\beta$ is ______.
40152.sol:
Time taken for one complete revolution = time period $= 2s$.

Therefore, $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \pirad{s}^{- 1}$

Now flux, $ϕ = NABcos ( \omegat )$

Therefore, induced EMF $ε = \left|- \dfrac{dϕ}{dt}\right| = NAB\omegasin ( \omegat )$

The maximum voltage generated, ${ε}_{max} = NAB\omega$

$= 200 \times 0 . 2 \times 0 . 01 \times \pi$

$= \dfrac{4\pi}{10} = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}$ volt

Hence, $\beta = 5$.

42123.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion (A) : Steel is used in the construction of buildings and bridges.
Reason (R) : Steel is more elastic and its elastic limit is high.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
$A$ is not correct but $R$ is correct
42123.sol:
The relationship between Young's modulus, stress, and strain is:

$\dfrac{stress}{strain} = Y$

Since the elastic modulus of steel is more, for the same amount of stress, the strain will be less resulting in less deformation of buildings and bridges. Therefore, steel is used for construction of large structures.

Hence, both assertion and reason are correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

42856.subject: Physics
42856.text: A rod of length $10$ cm lies along the principle axis of a concave mirror of focal length $10$ cm as shown in figure. The length of the image is _____ cm.
42856.sol:
For the given concave mirror, the focal length is $f = -10$ cm.

The rod lies along the principal axis. From the figure, the near end of the rod is at a distance of $20$ cm from the pole of the mirror. Since the length of the rod is $10$ cm, the far end is at a distance of $20 + 10 = 30$ cm from the pole.

Let the near end be $A$ and the far end be $B$.
Object distance for end $A$, $u_A = -20$ cm.
Object distance for end $B$, $u_B = -30$ cm.

Using the mirror formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

For end $A$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_A} + \dfrac{1}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{-10}$
$\dfrac{1}{v_A} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{10} = -\dfrac{1}{20}$
$v_A = -20$ cm

For end $B$:
$\dfrac{1}{v_B} + \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{-10}$
$\dfrac{1}{v_B} = \dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1 - 3}{30} = -\dfrac{2}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{15}$
$v_B = -15$ cm

The length of the image is the distance between the images of the two ends:
$\text{Length of image} = |v_A - v_B| = |-20 - (-15)| = |-5| = 5$ cm.

Answer: $5$

47266.subject: Biology
47266.text: BOD of polluted water is estimated by measuring the amount of _____
47266.sol:
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is defined as the amount of dissolved oxygen required by aerobic microorganisms to break down the organic matter present in a certain volume of a water sample.

To determine the BOD of polluted water, the dissolved oxygen (DO) of the sample is measured initially and then again after a standard incubation period (usually 5 days at $20^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$). The difference between the initial and final dissolved oxygen levels gives the amount of oxygen consumed by the microorganisms.

Therefore, BOD is estimated by measuring the amount of oxygen consumption.

Answer: Oxygen consumption

48698.text: If $3 x+y+k=0$ is a tangent to the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=10$, the values of $k$ are
48698.sol:
Given, line is $3 x+y+k=0$\Rightarrow \quad y=-3 x-k$ And equation of circle is x^{2}+y^{2}=10$
Here, $a^{2}=10, m=-3, c=-k$
If given line touches the circle, then length of intercept $=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sqrt{\frac{a^{2}\left(1+m^{2}\right)-c^{2}}{1+m^{2}}}=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sqrt{\frac{10(1+9)-k^{2}}{1+9}}=0\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{100-k^{2}}=0\Rightarrow \quad 100-k^{2}=0 \Rightarrow k=\pm 10$
Alternative : If the given line is tangent to the circle, then the length of the perpendicular from the centre upon the line is equal to the radius of the circle. $\begin{aligned}&\text{ i.e. } \quad\left|\frac{a x_{1}+b y_{1}+c}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\right|= r \\
&\Rightarrow \quad\left|\frac{3 \times 0+6 \times 0+k}{\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(1)^{2}}}\right|=\sqrt{10}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad\left|\frac{k}{\sqrt{10}}\right|=\sqrt{10}\\
&\Rightarrow \quad k=\sqrt{100} \Rightarrow k=\pm10
\end{aligned}
$

48739.subject: Mathematics
48739.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} ax + 7 & \text{if } x < 1 \\ 3x - 1 & \text{if } x = 1 \\ \dfrac{b}{x + 3} & \text{if } x > 1 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 1$, then
48739.sol:
For the function to be continuous at $x = 1$, the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and the value of the function at $x = 1$ must be equal.

$f(1) = 3(1) - 1 = 2$

$\lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} (ax + 7) = a + 7$

$\lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} \dfrac{b}{x + 3} = \dfrac{b}{4}$

Equating these values:

$a + 7 = 2 \Rightarrow a = -5$

$\dfrac{b}{4} = 2 \Rightarrow b = 8$

Answer: $a = -5, b = 8$

50862.text:
What is a period of revolution of earth satellite ? Ignore the height of satellite above the surface
of earth.
Given :
(1) The value of gravitational acceleration \( g=10 $\mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$\).
(2) Radius of earth \( R_{E}=6400 $\mathrm{ km}$\). Take \( \Pi=3.14 \).
50862.sol:
Given, gravitational acceleration, $g=10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$
radius of Earth, $R_{E}=6400 \mathrm{ km}=6400 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{ m}$
We know, period of revolution of Earth satellite is given as
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{R_{E}}{g}}=2 \times 3.14 \times \sqrt{\frac{6400 \times 10^{3}}{10}}=2 \times 3.14 \times 80 \times 10$
Therefore
$T=5024 \mathrm{ s}=\frac{5024}{60} \mathrm{ min}=83.733 \mathrm{ min}$
Thus, period of revolution of Earth satellite is $83.73$ minutes.

56630.text: What is the atomic number of first post actinoid element ?
56630.sol:
The actinoid series consists of elements with atomic numbers from $90$ to $103$.

The elements that follow the actinoid series are known as post-actinoid elements.

Therefore, the first post-actinoid element has an atomic number of $104$, which is Rutherfordium (Rf).

Answer: $104$

56634.subject: Chemistry
56634.text: What is the oxidation state of chromium in the final product when KI reacts with acidified potassium dichromate solution?
56634.sol:
Potassium dichromate (K_2Cr_2O_7$) acts as a strong oxidizing agent in an acidic medium.

It oxidizes iodide ions (I^-$) from KI to iodine (I_2$) and itself gets reduced to chromium(III) ions (Cr^{3+}$).

The ionic equation for the reaction is:

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6I^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 3I_2 + 7H_2O$

In the final product, chromium is present as $Cr^{3+}$.

Therefore, the oxidation state of chromium in the final product is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

58418.text: Which from following polymers is used to obtain surgical sutures?
58418.sol:
Surgical sutures require materials with high tensile strength, flexibility, and biocompatibility. Among common polymers, Nylon 6 (polyamide) possesses these properties and is widely employed as a non-absorbable suture material.

59765.subject: Chemistry
59765.text: Identify the gas adsorbed by solid to the largest extent at their respective critical temperature.
59765.sol:
The extent of adsorption of a gas on a solid surface depends on the strength of intermolecular forces. Gases with higher critical temperatures have stronger van der Waals forces of attraction and are more easily liquefiable, leading to a greater extent of adsorption.

The critical temperatures of the given gases are approximately:
$\text{H}_{2} \approx 33 \text{ K}$
$\text{N}_{2} \approx 126 \text{ K}$
$\text{O}_{2} \approx 154 \text{ K}$
$\text{SO}_{2} \approx 430 \text{ K}$

Since $\text{SO}_{2}$ has the highest critical temperature among the given options, it has the strongest intermolecular forces and is adsorbed to the largest extent.

Answer: $\text{SO}_{2(g)}$

64220.subject: Mathematics
64220.text: The circumradius of the triangle formed by the lines $x y+2 x+2 y+4=0$ and $x+y+2=0$ is
64220.sol:
The given equations of the lines are:

$xy + 2x + 2y + 4 = 0$

$x + y + 2 = 0$

Factor by grouping the first equation:

$x(y + 2) + 2(y + 2) = 0$

$(x + 2)(y + 2) = 0$

This represents two perpendicular lines: $x = -2$ and $y = -2$. The triangle is formed by the intersection of these lines with $x + y + 2 = 0$.

Finding the vertices from pairwise intersections:

Vertex A: $(-2,0)$ from $x = -2$ and $x + y + 2 = 0$

Vertex B: $(0,-2)$ from $y = -2$ and $x + y + 2 = 0$

Vertex C: $(-2,-2)$ from $x = -2$ and $y = -2$

The side lengths are:

$AB = \sqrt{(0 - (-2))^2 + (-2 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}$

$BC = \sqrt{(-2 - 0)^2 + (-2 - (-2))^2} = 2$

$CA = \sqrt{(-2 - (-2))^2 + (0 - (-2))^2} = 2$

We observe $BC^2 + CA^2 = 4 + 4 = 8 = AB^2$, so the triangle is right-angled with right angle at C.

The circumradius of a right triangle is half the hypotenuse length:

$R = \frac{AB}{2} = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} = \sqrt{2}$

The circumradius is $\sqrt{2} units.

$

66811.subject: Physics
66811.text: To manufacture a solenoid of length ' $\ell$ ' and inductance ' $L$ ', the length of the thin wire required is (Diameter of the solenoid is very less than length, $\mu_0=$ permeability of free space)
66811.sol:
The self-inductance of a long solenoid is given by $L = \mu_0 n^2 A \ell$, where $n$ is turns per unit length and $A$ is cross-sectional area.

Expressing $n = N/\ell$ and $A = \pi r^2$ yields $L = \mu_0 (N/\ell)^2 (\pi r^2) \ell = \mu_0 N^2 \pi r^2 / \ell$.

The wire length for $N$ turns of radius $r$ is $L_{wire} = 2\pi r N$, so $N = L_{wire}/(2\pi r)$.

Substituting gives $L = \frac{\mu_0}{\ell} \left(\frac{L_{wire}}{2\pi r}\right)^2 \pi r^2 = \frac{\mu_0 L_{wire}^2}{4\pi \ell}$.

Solving for $L_{wire}$ results in $L_{wire} = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi \ell L}{\mu_0}}$, matching option A.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

67404.text: 500 gram of a diatomic gas is enclosed at a pressure of $10^5 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$. The density of the gas is $5 \mathrm{kgm}^{-3}$. The energy of one mole of the gas due to its thermal motion is [consider the gas molecule as a rigid rotator]
67404.sol:
Energy of a diatomic gas due to thermal motion

The volume is obtained from the mass and density: $V = m / \rho = 0.5 \text{ kg} / 5 \text{ kg} \cdot \textm^{-3} = 0.1 \text{ m}^3$.

From the ideal gas law, $PV = nRT = 10^5 \text{ N} \cdot \textm^{-2} \times 0.1 \text{ m}^3 = 10^4 \text{ J}$.

A rigid diatomic molecule has five degrees of freedom: three translational and two rotational, so $f = 5$.

The internal energy becomes $U = \frac{5}{2} nRT = \frac{5}{2} \times 10^4 \text{ J} = 2.5 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$.

Since the problem refers to "the gas" and the mass is given, this result corresponds to the total internal energy of the sample, matching option B.

68701.text: Two particles 'A' and 'B' execute SHMs of periods 'T' and $'\left.\frac{3 T}{2}\right.'$. If they start from the mean position then the phase difference between them, when the particle 'A' completes two oscillations will be
68701.sol:
Given the periods $T_A = T$ and $T_B = \frac{3T}{2}$, both particles begin at the mean position with initial phase zero.

Particle A completes two oscillations after $t = 2T_A = 2T$ seconds.

The angular frequencies are $\omega_A = \frac{2\pi}{T_A} = \frac{2\pi}{T}$ and $\omega_B = \frac{2\pi}{T_B} = \frac{4\pi}{3T}$.

At $t = 2T$, their phases are:

$\phi_A = \omega_A t = \frac{2\pi}{T} \cdot 2T = 4\pi$

$\phi_B = \omega_B t = \frac{4\pi}{3T} \cdot 2T = \frac{8\pi}{3}$

The phase difference is:

$\Delta\phi = \left|4\pi - \frac{8\pi}{3}\right| = \frac{4\pi}{3}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

69164.subject: Physics
69164.text: $A solid sphere of mass M and a disc of mass \dfrac{M}{2}$ have the same radius. The ratio of moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane to the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent will be
69164.sol:
Let the radius of the solid sphere and the disc be $R$.

Mass of the solid sphere, $m_{s} = M$

Mass of the disc, $m_{d} = \dfrac{M}{2}$

Moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $\dfrac{1}{4}m_{d}R^2$. Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane is:

$I_{disc} = \dfrac{1}{4}m_{d}R^2 + m_{d}R^2 = \dfrac{5}{4}m_{d}R^2$

Substituting $m_{d} = \dfrac{M}{2}$:

$I_{disc} = \dfrac{5}{4}\left(\dfrac{M}{2}\right)R^2 = \dfrac{5}{8}MR^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its diameter is $\dfrac{2}{5}m_{s}R^2$. Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its tangent is:

$I_{sphere} = \dfrac{2}{5}m_{s}R^2 + m_{s}R^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}m_{s}R^2$

Substituting $m_{s} = M$:

$I_{sphere} = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$

The required ratio is:

$\dfrac{I_{disc}}{I_{sphere}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{8}MR^2}{\dfrac{7}{5}MR^2} = \dfrac{5}{8} \times \dfrac{5}{7} = \dfrac{25}{56}$

Answer: $25 : 56$

69763.text: For a perfectly black body, coefficient of emission is
69763.sol:
Perfect black body absorption and emission

A perfectly black body absorbs all incident radiation regardless of wavelength, giving it an absorption coefficient $a = 1$.

Kirchhoff's law establishes that emissivity equals absorptivity at a given wavelength and temperature: $e = a$.

Since $a = 1$, the emissivity must also be unity: $e = 1$.

A perfectly black body is therefore both a perfect absorber and perfect emitter of radiation.

The correct choice is $\boxed{B}$.

69972.subject: Physics
69972.text: A monoatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure. The percentage of total heat used in increasing the internal energy and that used for doing external work is A and B respectively. Then the ratio, $\mathrm{A}: \mathrm{B}$ is
69972.sol:
The first law of thermodynamics states that $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$, where $\Delta Q$ is the heat supplied, $\Delta U$ is the change in internal energy, and $\Delta W$ is the work done by the gas.

For a monoatomic ideal gas undergoing a constant pressure process, the quantities are given by $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$ with $C_v = \frac{3}{2} R$, $\Delta W = n R \Delta T$, and $\Delta Q = n C_p \Delta T$ with $C_p = \frac{5}{2} R$.

The percentage of heat used to increase internal energy is:

$A = \frac{\Delta U}{\Delta Q} \times 100 = \frac{n (3R/2) \Delta T}{n (5R/2) \Delta T} \times 100 = \frac{3}{5} \times 100 = 60\%$

The percentage used for external work is:

$B = \frac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} \times 100 = \frac{n R \Delta T}{n (5R/2) \Delta T} \times 100 = \frac{2}{5} \times 100 = 40\%$

Therefore, the ratio $A : B = 60 : 40 = 3 : 2$, and the correct choice is C.

70438.subject: Physics
70438.text: A progressive wave of frequency 50 Hz is travelling with velocity 350 m/s through a medium. The change in phase at given time interval of 0.01s is
70438.sol:
Given frequency $f = 50\text{ Hz}$

Time interval $\Delta t = 0.01\text{ s}$

The phase of a progressive wave at a fixed position varies with time as $\phi = \omega t - kx + \phi_0$

The change in phase over a time interval $\Delta t$ is given by $\Delta \phi = \omega \Delta t$

Since $\omega = 2\pi f$, we have:

$\Delta \phi = 2\pi f \Delta t$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta \phi = 2\pi \times 50 \times 0.01$

$\Delta \phi = 100\pi \times 0.01 = \pi\text{ rad}$

Answer: $\pi\,\text{rad}$

71196.subject: Biology
71196.text: The true mature ovum in human female with its vitelline membrane in contact with the sperm head shows the following features EXCEPT:
options: Its centriole develops the synkaryon spindle.
71196.sol:
In human females, the secondary oocyte is arrested in metaphase II of meiosis. When the sperm head comes in contact with the vitelline membrane, it triggers the completion of meiotic division II, resulting in the formation of a mature ovum and a second polar body.

At this stage, the ovum contains a female pronucleus and shows two polar bodies (the first polar body formed after meiosis I and the second after meiosis II).

However, the mature human ovum lacks a functional centriole. The proximal centriole is introduced by the sperm during fertilization, and it is this sperm centriole that divides and develops the synkaryon spindle for the first cleavage division. Therefore, the statement that the ovum's centriole develops the synkaryon spindle is incorrect.

Answer: Its centriole develops the synkaryon spindle.

71316.subject: Biology
71316.text: Intrinsic plasticity is observed in the leaves of __________.
71316.sol:
Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity.

Intrinsic plasticity (developmental heterophylly) is the phenomenon where the leaves of a juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. This is observed in cotton, coriander, and larkspur.

Extrinsic plasticity (environmental heterophylly) is the phenomenon where the shape of leaves differs based on the environment, such as leaves produced in air versus those produced in water. This is observed in buttercup.

Therefore, intrinsic plasticity is observed in coriander.

Answer: coriander

71530.subject: Biology
71530.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
71530.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I - There is no need of agitation in callus culture however it is necessary in suspension culture.
Statement II - During tissue culture techniques, the temperature of the lab is maintained between 18 to 20°C.
In the light of above statements, select the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
71530.sol:
Statement I is correct because callus culture is typically grown on a solid agar medium where agitation is not required. In contrast, suspension culture involves growing cells in a liquid medium, which requires continuous agitation (usually on a rotary shaker) to ensure proper aeration, nutrient mixing, and to prevent the aggregation of cells.

Statement II is incorrect because the standard temperature maintained in a plant tissue culture laboratory is generally around $24^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$ to $28^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$ (often specified as $25 \pm 2^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$), not $18$ to $20^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.

71677.subject: Chemistry
71677.text: Identify the structure of alanine when pH is $11$.
71677.sol:
Alanine is an amino acid with an acidic carboxyl group and a basic amino group.

In a highly basic medium at pH $11$, the solution provides a large concentration of $\text{OH}^-$ ions.

Both the carboxyl group and the protonated amino group will lose their protons.

The $-\text{COOH}$ group deprotonates to form $-\text{COO}^-$, and the $-\text{NH}_3^+$ group deprotonates to form $-\text{NH}_2$.

Thus, alanine exists as an anion with the structure $\text{NH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-COO}^-$.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-COO}^-$

71958.subject: Chemistry
71958.text: Calculate the atomic radius of an element having edge length $3.61 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$ for fcc structure.
71958.sol:
For a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, the atoms touch each other along the face diagonal.

The relationship between the edge length $a$ and the atomic radius $r$ is given by:

$4r = \sqrt{2}a$

$r = \dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Given $a = 3.61 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$.

Substituting the value of $a$:

$r = \dfrac{3.61 \times 10^{-8}}{2 \times 1.414}$

$r = \dfrac{3.61 \times 10^{-8}}{2.828}$

$r = 1.276 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm} \approx 1.28 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$

Answer: $1.28 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$

72120.subject: Physics
72120.text: The amount of work done in increasing voltage across the plates of capacitor from 5 V to 10 V is W. The work done in increasing it from 10 V to 20 V is
72120.sol:
The work done in increasing the voltage across a capacitor is equal to the change in its electrostatic potential energy.

$W = \Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} C (V_f^2 - V_i^2)$

For the first case, the voltage increases from $5$ V to $10$ V:

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} C (10^2 - 5^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} C (100 - 25) = \dfrac{75}{2} C$

For the second case, the voltage increases from $10$ V to $20$ V:

$W' = \dfrac{1}{2} C (20^2 - 10^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} C (400 - 100) = \dfrac{300}{2} C$

Taking the ratio of the two work done values:

$\dfrac{W'}{W} = \dfrac{300}{75} = 4$

$W' = 4W$

Answer: $4W$

72309.subject: Physics
72309.text: For a radioactive nucleus that undergoes $\beta^+$ decay, which of the following CANNOT occur?
options: Nuclei with lower atomic number than that of original nucleus is produced.
The proton is converted to neutron
Isobar of original nucleus is produced.
Isotope of original nucleus is produced.
72309.sol:
In $\beta^+$ decay, a proton inside the nucleus is converted into a neutron, a positron, and an electron neutrino. The nuclear reaction is represented as:

^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow ^{A}_{Z-1}Y + e^+ + \nu_e$

The atomic number $Z$ decreases by 1$, so a nucleus with a lower atomic number is produced.

The mass number $A$ remains unchanged, meaning the daughter nucleus is an isobar of the original nucleus.

Since the atomic number changes, the daughter nucleus cannot be an isotope of the original nucleus, as isotopes must have the same atomic number.

Answer: Isotope of original nucleus is produced.

77100.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The general solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+x$ is of the form $y=g(x)+c$, where $c$ is an arbitrary constant.
2. The degree of $\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=f(x)$ is 2 .
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
77100.sol:
Statement 1:
The general solution of $\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+x$ Now integrating on both side
$\int \frac{d y}{d x}=\int[f(x)+x] d x\therefore \quad y=f(x)+C\therefore \quad$ Statement 1 is correct.
Statement 2:
$\frac{d y}{d x}=f(x)+c$
Squaring both sides,
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=(f(x)+c)^2 \\
& \left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2=\left[f(x)^2+2 \mathrm{cf}(x)+c^2\right]
\end{aligned}$
Hence, the differential equation is of order -1 and degree -2 .
$\therefore \quad$ both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
$\therefore \quad$ Option (C) is correct.

77301.subject: Mathematics
77301.text:
Passage: Consider the curves $y=x^2$ and $y=2|x|$.

Question: What is the number of points of intersection of the curves ?
77301.sol:
Equating the two given curves $y = x^2$ and $y = 2|x|$:

$x^2 = 2|x|$

Since $x^2 = |x|^2$, the equation becomes:

$|x|^2 - 2|x| = 0$

$|x|(|x| - 2) = 0$

This gives $|x| = 0$ or $|x| = 2$.

Solving for $x$, we get $x = 0$, $x = 2$, and $x = -2$.

The corresponding points of intersection are $(0,0)$, $(2,4)$, and $(-2,4)$.

The number of points of intersection is $3$.

Answer: $3$

78351.subject: Mathematics
78351.text: The sum of the first $k$ terms of a series $S$ is $3k^2 + 5k$. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The terms of $S$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference 14.
The terms of $S$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference 6.
The terms of $S$ form a geometric progression with common ratio $\dfrac{10}{7}$.
The terms of $S$ form a geometric progression with common ratio $\dfrac{11}{4}$.
78351.sol:
The sum of the first $k$ terms of the series is given by $S_k = 3k^2 + 5k$.

The $k$-th term of the series, $T_k$, is obtained by subtracting the sum of the first $k-1$ terms from the sum of the first $k$ terms:

$T_k = S_k - S_{k-1}$

Substituting the given expression for $S_k$ and $S_{k-1}$:

$T_k = (3k^2 + 5k) - [3(k-1)^2 + 5(k-1)]$

$T_k = 3k^2 + 5k - [3(k^2 - 2k + 1) + 5k - 5]$

$T_k = 3k^2 + 5k - (3k^2 - 6k + 3 + 5k - 5)$

$T_k = 3k^2 + 5k - (3k^2 - k - 2)$

$T_k = 6k + 2$

To find the common difference, we calculate the difference between consecutive terms:

$T_k - T_{k-1} = (6k + 2) - [6(k-1) + 2]$

$T_k - T_{k-1} = 6k + 2 - (6k - 6 + 2)$

$T_k - T_{k-1} = 6$

Since the difference between consecutive terms is a constant, the terms of the series form an arithmetic progression with a common difference of 6.

Answer: The terms of $S$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference 6.

84183.subject: Zoology
84183.text: When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration in blood increases breathing becomes:
options: there is no effect on breathing
84183.sol:
When $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration in blood increases breathing becomes faster and deeper. The effect of increased $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is to decrease the affinity of haemoglobin for $\mathrm{O}_2$. Thus, due to Bohr's effect the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ released in respiring tissue accelerates the delivery of oxygen by faster and deeper breathing.
Related Theory
Bohr and Haldane's effect are two properties of haemoglobin. They help the dissociation of respiratory gases from the haemoglobin molecule based on the physiological conditions of their final destination. Bohr effect is the decrease of the oxygen binding capacity of haemoglobin with the increase of the concentration of carbon dioxide or decrease in $\mathrm{pH}$ whereas Haldane effect is the decrease of the carbon dioxide binding capacity of haemoglobin with the rise in the concentration of oxygen. Furthermore, Bohr effect aids in the release of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin at the metabolizing tissues while Haldane effect aids in the release of carbon dioxide from carboxyhaemoglobin in the lungs.

84978.subject: Zoology
84978.text: Protein Synthesis in an animal cell occurs:
options: only on the ribosomes present in cytosol
only on ribosome attached to the nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum
on ribosome present in the nucleolus as well as in cytoplasm
on ribosomes present in cytoplasm as well as in mitochondria.
84978.sol:
Ribosomes are known as protein factory and are actively involved in the synthesis of protein. Ribosomes are found in the cytosol and in the semi-autonomous organelles, such as mitochondria and chloroplasts.
Related Theory
Ribosomes either occur singly (monosomes) or in cluster (polysomes). Apart from ribosomal RNA (rRNA), the other two forms of RNA required for protein synthesis are: messenger $R N A$ (mRNA), which carries coding information from DNA, and transfer RNA (tRNA), which carries amino acids. Ribosomes use the information in $m R N A$ to direct the synthesis of a protein. In prokaryotes, during proteins synthesis, many ribosomes line up and join the $m R N A$ to form a string of ribosomes called polyribosome or polysome.

85321.subject: Zoology
85321.text: One of the parents of a cross has a mutation in its mitochondria. In that cross, that parent is taken as male. During segregation of $\mathrm{F}_2$ progenies that mutation is found in:
85321.sol:
Cytoplasmic inheritance or extranuclear inheritance is the transmission of genes that occur outside the nucleus such as mitochondria and chloroplasts or from cellular parasites like viruses or bacteria. In mammals, cytoplasmic genes are only contributed by female gamete, e.g., Male gamete only contribute its nuclear genes. Thus, none progenies would not inherit any mutated genes in mitochondria by father.
Related Theory
The phenotypes that are controlled by nuclear factors found in the cytoplasm of the female are said to express a maternal effect. Those phenotypes controlled by organelle genes exhibit maternal inheritance. The classic phenotype which exhibits maternal effects is coiling direction of snail shells.

89799.text: The acute angle of intersection of the curves $x^{2}y = 1$ and $y = x^{2}$ in the first quadrant is $\theta,$ then $tan ⁡ \theta$& is equal to

Solving the equation of the curves, we get
$\dfrac{1}{x^{2}} = x^{2} ⇒ x = \pm 1$
$∴$ Intersection point is $\left(1,1\right)$ in the first quadrant.
Now, $x^{2}y = 1 ⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{x^{2}}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- 2}{x^{3}}$
$⇒ {m}_{1} = - 2$~(by putting $x = 1$)
And $y = x^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x$
$⇒ {m}_{2} = 2$

90652.text: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{xy}{1 - {x}^{2}} = x\sqrt{y},$ $\left(\left|x\right| < 1\right)$ is $\sqrt{y} = - \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{3} + C\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4},$ where $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and $C$  is an arbitrary constant. Then, the value of $f\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ is
90652.sol:
Given equation is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{1 - {x}^{2}}\sqrt{y} = x$
Let, $2\sqrt{y} = ν$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dν}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dν}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{2\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}ν = x$
$∴$ I.F. $= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{x}{2\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}dx}$
$= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{- d\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}{4\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}}$
$= {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}ln\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}$
$= {\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}$
Thus, the solution is $ν{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}} = ∫ x{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}}dx$
or $ν ⋅ {\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{4}} = - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{4} + {C}^{'}$
or $2\sqrt{y} = - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right) + {C}^{'}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4}$
$⇒ \sqrt{y} = - \dfrac{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}{3} + C{\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{4}}$
$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 1 - {x}^{2}$
$⇒ f\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

92348.sol:

$\cos^{2} ⁡ x + cos ⁡ x - 1 = 0$

$= \left(1 - \left(\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)\right)\left(2 - \left(\dfrac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)\right)$
$= \dfrac{\left(2 - 3 + \sqrt{5}\right)}{2}\dfrac{\left(4 - 3 + \sqrt{5}\right)}{2}$
$= \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{5} - 1\right)}{2}\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{5} + 1\right)}{2} = \dfrac{4}{4} = 1$

92673.text: In a one dimensional collision between two identical particles $A$ and $B$, $B$ is stationary and $A$ has momentum $p$ before impact. During impact $B$ gives an impulse $J$ to $A$. Then the coefficient of restitution between the two is
92673.sol:
Let ${p}_{1}$ and ${p}_{2}$ be the momenta of $A$ and $B$ after collision.



Then applying impulse = change in linear momentum for the two particles

For $B: J = {p}_{1} \ldots ( i )$

For $A: J = p - {p}_{2}$

Or ${p}_{2} = p - J \ldots ( ii )$

Coefficient of restitution $e = \dfrac{{P}_{1} - {P}_{2}}{P}$

$= \dfrac{{p}_{1} - p + J}{p}$

$= \dfrac{J - p + J}{p} = \dfrac{2J}{p} - 1$

$\left|\text{\Delta} \overset{→}{P}\right| = \text{m} \sqrt{\dfrac{v^{2}}{4} + \text{u} {}^{2} - \text{uv} + \dfrac{3 v^{2}}{4}}$

$\text{impulse} = \text{m} \sqrt{v^{2} + \text{u} {}^{2} - \text{uv}}$

97463.text: Normally algae show a haplontic life cycle. Polysiphonia and Fucus are exceptions to this rule. The correct option depicting their classes and life cycles is
options: Polysiphonia is a green alga with haplo-diplontic life cycle and Fucus is a red alga with diplontic life cycle

97463.sol:
The diplontic life cycle is a cycle in which the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to the few-celled haploid gametophyte. It is seen in all seed-bearing plants gymnosperms and angiosperms. It is also seen in the brown alga Fucus.

Haplo-diplontic life cycle is a cycle in which a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid, or erect phase is represented by a haploid gametophyte, and it alternates with the short-lived, multicellular sporophyte totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte. This is seen in bryophytes, in the brown alga Ectocarpus and the red algae Polysiphonia

100104.subject: Physics
100104.text: The force $F$ acting on a particle is given by the equation $F = \dfrac{\alpha - x^2}{\beta t}$, where $x$ is distance and $t$ is time. The dimensional formula of the ratio $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$ is:
100104.sol:
According to the principle of dimensional homogeneity, quantities added or subtracted must have the same dimensions.

Therefore, the dimensions of $\alpha$ must be the same as those of $x^2$.
$[\alpha] = [x^2] = [\mathrm{L}^2]$

The dimensional formula for the entire equation is:
$[F] = \dfrac{[\alpha]}{[\beta][t]}$

Rearranging to find the dimensions of $\beta$:
$[\beta] = \dfrac{[\alpha]}{[F][t]} = \dfrac{[\mathrm{L}^2]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-2}][\mathrm{T}]}$
$[\beta] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{L}^2]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-1}]} = [\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}]$

Now, the dimensional formula of the ratio $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$ is:
$\left[\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}\right] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{L}^2]}{[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}]} = [\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-1}]$

Answer: $[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-1}]$

100354.subject: Physics
100354.text: A drone flies parallel to a double railway track. Trains depart from stations at both ends of the track every $T$ minutes, moving at a constant speed of $80 \text{ km/h}$ in both directions. The drone meets a train moving in the opposite direction every $12 \text{ minutes}$, and overtakes a train moving in the same direction every $36 \text{ minutes}$. What is the speed of the drone and the time period $T$ of the train service?
100354.sol:
Let the speed of the drone be $v_d$ and the distance between two consecutive trains be $d$.

Since the trains depart every $T$ minutes at a speed of $v_t = 80 \text{ km/h}$, the distance between them is:
$d = v_t \times T = 80 \times \dfrac{T}{60}$ (with $T$ in minutes and $d$ in km)

For trains moving in the opposite direction, the relative speed is $v_d + 80$. The time interval between encounters is $12 \text{ min}$ ($\dfrac{1}{5} \text{ h}$).
$d = (v_d + 80) \times \dfrac{1}{5}$

For trains moving in the same direction, the drone overtakes them, so the relative speed is $v_d - 80$. The time interval is $36 \text{ min}$ ($\dfrac{3}{5} \text{ h}$).
$d = (v_d - 80) \times \dfrac{3}{5}$

Equating the two expressions for $d$:
$(v_d + 80) \times \dfrac{1}{5} = (v_d - 80) \times \dfrac{3}{5}$
$v_d + 80 = 3v_d - 240$
$2v_d = 320 \Rightarrow v_d = 160 \text{ km/h}$

Substitute $v_d$ back to find $d$:
$d = (160 + 80) \times \dfrac{1}{5} = 48 \text{ km}$

Finally, find the time period $T$:
$T = \dfrac{d}{v_t} = \dfrac{48}{80} \text{ h} = 0.6 \text{ h} = 36 \text{ min}$

Answer: $160 \text{ km/h}, 36 \text{ min}$

102789.subject: Physics
102789.text:
Statement-I : Coulombic force follows the principle of superposition.
and
Statement-II : Coulombic force is directly proportional to the charges on both particle.
options: Statement-I is True, Statement-II is True; Statement-II is a correct explanation for Statement-I.
Statement-I is True, Statement-II is True; Statement-II is not a correct explanation for Statement-I.
Statement-I is True, Statement-II is False.
Statement-I is False, Statement-II is True.
102789.sol:
Statement-I:
Coulombic force follows the principle of superposition.
- This statement is True. The principle of superposition states that the total force acting on a charge due to multiple other charges is the vector sum of the individual forces exerted by each charge separately.
Statement-II:
Coulombic force is directly proportional to the charges on both particles.
- This statement is True. According to Coulomb's law, the force \(F\) between two point charges \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) is given by the formula:
\(F=k \frac{\left|q_1 q_2\right|}{r^2}\)
Conclusion:
- Statement I is true and Statement II is true. However, Statement II does not explain Statement I. The principle of superposition is about how forces combine, whereas Statement II describes the proportionality of the force to the charges.
Therefore, the correct answer is: (2) Statement-I is True, Statement-II is True; Statement-II is not a correct explanation for Statement-I.

104458.subject: Physics
104458.text: A point object is placed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$. A convex mirror of radius of curvature $40\text{ cm}$ is placed coaxially at a distance of $40\text{ cm}$ behind the lens. The position of the final image formed after reflection from the mirror and subsequent refraction through the lens is:
options: $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object
$60\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side opposite to the object
$60\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object
104458.sol:
For the first refraction through the convex lens:
$u_1 = -30\text{ cm}$, $f_L = +20\text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_L}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{60}$

$v_1 = +60\text{ cm}$

The first image is formed $60\text{ cm}$ behind the lens. Since the convex mirror is placed $40\text{ cm}$ behind the lens, this image acts as a virtual object for the mirror, located $20\text{ cm}$ behind it.

For the reflection from the convex mirror:
$u_M = +20\text{ cm}$ (virtual object)
The focal length of the convex mirror is $f_M = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{+40\text{ cm}}{2} = +20\text{ cm}$.

Using the mirror formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v_M} + \dfrac{1}{u_M} = \dfrac{1}{f_M}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_M} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v_M} = 0$

$v_M = \infty$

The rays reflected by the convex mirror become parallel to the principal axis.

For the second refraction through the convex lens:
The parallel rays ($u_2 = -\infty$) fall on the lens and will converge at its principal focus.

$v_2 = f_L = 20\text{ cm}$

Since the light is now traveling in the reverse direction (from the mirror to the lens), the final image is formed $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the original object.

Answer: $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens on the side of the object

104467.subject: Physics
104467.text: An equilateral prism made of a material of refractive index $2$ is completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$. A ray of monochromatic light is incident on one face of the prism such that the refracted ray inside the prism travels parallel to its base. What is the angle of incidence of the ray at the prism face?
104467.sol:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$.

When the refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to its base, the prism is in the position of minimum deviation.

In this position, the angle of refraction at the first face is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$.

Applying Snell's law at the first refracting surface, we use the relative refractive index of the prism with respect to the surrounding liquid:

$\mu_{\text{liquid}} \sin i = \mu_{\text{prism}} \sin r$

Substituting the given values ($\mu_{\text{liquid}} = \sqrt{2}$, $\mu_{\text{prism}} = 2$):

$\sqrt{2} \sin i = 2 \sin 30^\circ$

$\sqrt{2} \sin i = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$

$\sin i = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore, the angle of incidence is $i = 45^\circ$.

Answer: $45^\circ$

104951.text:
Assertion (A): Amongst \(\alpha, \beta\) and \(\gamma\)-particles, \(\alpha\)-particle has maximum penetrating power.
Reason (R): The \(\alpha\)-particle is heavier than \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\)-particle.

Both \(A\) and \(R\) are true, but \(R\) is not the correct explanation of \(A\).
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
104951.sol: The correct option is (4). Alpha particles have the least penetrating power due to their larger mass and charge, which causes them to interact more strongly with matter and lose energy quickly. Gamma rays have the maximum penetrating power because they are electromagnetic radiation with no charge and no rest mass, allowing them to pass through matter with minimal interaction. While the alpha particle is indeed heavier than beta and gamma particles, this heaviness is precisely why it has low penetrating power, not maximum.

105129.text: In radioactive decay process, the negatively charged emitted $\beta$-particles are
options: the electrons present inside the nucleus
the electrons produced as a result of the decay of neutrons inside the nucleus
the electrons produced as a result of collisions between atoms
the electrons orbiting around the nucleus
105129.sol:
Beta decay can involve the emission of either electrons or positrons. The electrons or positrons emitted in a $\beta$-decay do not exist inside the nucleus. They are only created at the time of emission, just as photons are created when an atom makes a transition from higher to a lower energy state.
In negative $\beta$-decay a neutron in the nucleus is transformed into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino. Hence, in radioactive decay process, the negatively charged emitted $\beta$-particles are the electrons produced as a result of the decay of neutrons present inside the nucleus.

105539.subject: Physics
105539.text: Photons of energy $E$ are incident on two different photosensitive surfaces X and Y. The work functions of the surfaces are $\phi_X$ and $\phi_Y$ respectively, where $\phi_X < \phi_Y < E$. If $\lambda_X$ and $\lambda_Y$ are the minimum de Broglie wavelengths of the emitted photoelectrons from surfaces X and Y respectively, which of the following statements is correct regarding their relationship initially, and the effect on the ratio $\lambda_X/\lambda_Y$ if the incident photon energy $E$ is doubled?
105539.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is $K = E - \phi$.

Since $\phi_X < \phi_Y$, it follows that $K_X > K_Y$.

The minimum de Broglie wavelength of the photoelectrons is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$.

Because $K_X > K_Y$, we have $\lambda_X < \lambda_Y$.

The ratio of the wavelengths is $\dfrac{\lambda_X}{\lambda_Y} = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_Y}{K_X}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{E - \phi_Y}{E - \phi_X}}$.

When the incident energy $E$ is doubled to $2E$, the new ratio becomes $\sqrt{\dfrac{2E - \phi_Y}{2E - \phi_X}}$.

For any positive fraction where the numerator is less than the denominator, adding the same positive amount to both (or scaling $E$ up) brings the fraction closer to 1. Thus, the value of $\dfrac{E - \phi_Y}{E - \phi_X}$ increases as $E$ increases.

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{\lambda_X}{\lambda_Y}$ increases.

Answer: $\lambda_X < \lambda_Y$, and the ratio $\lambda_X/\lambda_Y$ increases

107771.subject: Chemistry
107771.text: Which of the following diatomic molecules has a bond order of 2 consisting entirely of $\pi$ bonds, and what is the correct molecular orbital energy justification for this?
options: $\text{C}_2$, because the energy of the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals is lower than that of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital.
$\text{C}_2$, because the energy of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital is lower than that of the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals.
$\text{O}_2$, because the presence of electrons in the $\pi^{*}_{2p_x}$ and $\pi^{*}_{2p_y}$ orbitals cancels the $\sigma$ bond.
$\text{N}_2$, because it has a triple bond and the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital is highest in energy among the bonding orbitals.
107771.sol:
The electronic configuration of the $\text{C}_2$ molecule (12 electrons) is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \, \sigma^{*}_{1s}^2 \, \sigma_{2s}^2 \, \sigma^{*}_{2s}^2 \, \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2$.

For molecules with 14 or fewer electrons (like $\text{C}_2$), $2\text{s}-2\text{p}$ mixing causes the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital to be higher in energy than the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals.

Because the last four valence electrons fill the degenerate $\pi$ orbitals while leaving the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital empty, the bond order is $\dfrac{8-4}{2} = 2$, and both bonds are $\pi$ bonds.

If $\sigma_{2p_z}$ were lower in energy, the molecule would have one $\sigma$ and one $\pi$ bond instead.

Answer: $\text{C}_2$, because the energy of the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals is lower than that of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital.

113908.subject: Chemistry
113908.text: What mass of urea (molar mass $= 60 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$) must be dissolved in $90 \text{ g}$ of water to reduce the vapour pressure of water by $25\%$?
113908.sol:
Let the mass of urea be $w \text{ g}$.

Moles of urea, $n_{\text{solute}} = \dfrac{w}{60}$

Moles of water, $n_{\text{solvent}} = \dfrac{90}{18} = 5 \text{ mol}$

Relative lowering of vapour pressure is equal to the mole fraction of the solute:
$\dfrac{\Delta P}{P^0} = X_{\text{solute}}$

Given that the vapour pressure is reduced by $25\%$, the relative lowering is $0.25$.

$0.25 = \dfrac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solute}} + n_{\text{solvent}}}$

$\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solute}} + 5}$

$n_{\text{solute}} + 5 = 4 n_{\text{solute}}$

$3 n_{\text{solute}} = 5 \Rightarrow n_{\text{solute}} = \dfrac{5}{3} \text{ mol}$

Mass of urea, $w = \dfrac{5}{3} \times 60 = 100 \text{ g}$

Answer: $100 \text{ g}$

118806.subject: Chemistry
118806.text: An unknown alcohol with the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ is treated with Lucas reagent at room temperature. It produces turbidity immediately. The IUPAC name of the unknown alcohol is:
118806.sol:
The Lucas test is used to distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. The reagent is a mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.

The formation of turbidity is due to the formation of an insoluble alkyl chloride. Tertiary alcohols react immediately to form turbidity, secondary alcohols take about 5 minutes, and primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Since the unknown alcohol ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) produces turbidity immediately, it must be a tertiary alcohol.

Among the structural isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$:
Bu\tan^{-1}-ol is a primary alcohol.
Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol.
2-Methylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol.
2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol.

Therefore, the unknown alcohol is 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

Answer: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

121553.subject: Botany
121553.text:
In the earlier two-kingdom classification system, Chlamydomonas (having a cell wall) and Amoeba (lacking a cell wall) were placed in separate kingdoms. However, in R.H. Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, they are placed together in Kingdom Protista.

Which of the following criteria proposed by Whittaker primarily justify bringing these two organisms together into the same kingdom?
options: Mode of nutrition and presence of cell wall
Phylogenetic relationships and mode of reproduction
Cell structure and mode of nutrition
121553.sol:
In the earlier classification systems, Chlamydomonas was placed with plants (due to the presence of a cell wall) and Amoeba was placed with animals (due to the absence of a cell wall).

Whittaker's five-kingdom classification groups organisms based on specific criteria such as cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

Kingdom Protista was created exclusively for all single-celled (unicellular) eukaryotes. Both Chlamydomonas and Amoeba share a eukaryotic cell structure and a cellular body organisation (being unicellular). This shared cellular complexity is the primary reason they are grouped together in Protista, despite their differences in cell wall presence and mode of nutrition (Chlamydomonas is autotrophic, while Amoeba is heterotrophic).

Answer: Cell structure and body organisation

123526.subject: Botany
123526.text: How is a structure consisting of millions of cells formed?
options: By growth and division of a single parental cell and its progeny
By formation of new cells from dormant cells
By combination of different cell types
123526.sol: Are you aware that all organisms, even the largest, start their life from a single cell? You may wonder how a single cell then goes on to form such large organisms. Growth and reproduction are characteristics of cells, indeed of all living organisms. All cells reproduce by dividing into two, with each parental cell giving rise to two daughter cells each time they divide. These newly formed daughter cells can themselves grow and divide, giving rise to a new cell population that is formed by the growth and division of a single parental cell and its progeny. In other words, such cycles of growth and division allow a single cell to form a structure consisting of millions of cells.

options: It consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of $0.5 \mu\text{m}$ to $1.0 \mu\text{m}$ diameter.
The cis and trans faces of the organelle are entirely different but interconnected.
The forming face is convex in shape while the maturing face is concave.
Vesicles from the ER fuse with the trans face and move towards the forming face.
124358.sol:
The Golgi apparatus consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of $0.5 \mu\text{m}$ to $1.0 \mu\text{m}$ diameter. Its forming (cis) face is convex and the maturing (trans) face is concave. These two faces are entirely different but interconnected.

Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis (forming) face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing (trans) face. Therefore, the statement claiming that vesicles fuse with the trans face and move towards the forming face is incorrect.

Answer: Vesicles from the ER fuse with the trans face and move towards the forming face.
